world: Kestrelwick Systems, Inc. is a fictional company of about 310 people in Duluth, Minnesota (hub in Chattanooga, Tennessee) that builds Coldline, a routing and temperature-compliance platform for refrigerated freight. It is hiring one role, Engineering Lead, Ingestion Platform (requisition ENG-2026-0417), a people-manager role reporting to Idris Halvorsen-Peake, Director of Data Platform. The user is the recruiter, Pernille Aubrecht, running the recruiter screen in early October 2026. The other party is the candidate, Ottoline Vaskirk, currently Engineering Team Lead at the fictional Halcyard Freight Cloud in Madison, Wisconsin. The pack holds the approved job description, her resume, the interview scorecard, a candidate-shareable team brief, the current Total Rewards overview (version 4.1, 2026), last year's Total Rewards overview (version 3.2, 2025, outdated, distinguishable only by its version and date), the engineering recruiting process guide, and the hiring manager's informal notes, which conflict with the job description on on-call. The scorecard and the process guide, both current, genuinely disagree on the panel decision rule.

files.title: Job description: Engineering Lead, Ingestion Platform (ENG-2026-0417)

facts.statement: The role is Engineering Lead, Ingestion Platform at Kestrelwick Systems, requisition ENG-2026-0417, full-time and exempt.
The posted base salary range for the role is $172,000 to $198,000 per year.
The role's location is Duluth, Minnesota.
The job description is version 1.2, approved on 1 September 2026 and posted on 3 September 2026.
The lead is expected to spend roughly 60% of the week on people and delivery leadership and 40% on hands-on work.
The Engineering Lead line-manages the engineers on the Ingestion Platform team (1:1s, growth plans, performance reviews, hiring); the job description gives no headcount.
The team's ingestion service-level objective is 99.9% of device messages processed within 60 seconds.
The lead takes part in the team's on-call rotation and carries the pager one week in five.
The lead acts as incident commander for ingestion incidents and runs the review that follows.
The role travels to the Chattanooga hub for planning weeks, up to four trips per year.
doc_needles: up to four trips per year

facts.statement: Required: 7 or more years building backend or data-intensive systems that ran in production.
Required: at least 2 years of direct people management including hiring and performance reviews; mentoring or tech-lead work without line responsibility does not count.
Required: hands-on production experience operating a log-based streaming platform such as Kafka, Pulsar or Redpanda.
doc_needles: log-based streaming platform such as Kafka

facts.statement: Required: experience leading the response to an incident on a customer-facing service as incident commander.
Required: fluency in a compiled backend language; the team works mostly in Go.
Nice to have (not required): telematics or IoT device data, change data capture pipelines, managing the cost of cloud data infrastructure, multi-region active-active deployments.
Where an offer lands inside the range depends on experience and on internal equity.
The role is eligible for an annual bonus and a new-hire equity grant; the job description gives no figures for either and points to the Total Rewards overview.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and the posting stays open until the role is filled.
The working arrangement for the role follows the company location policy; the job description itself does not say how many office days or whether remote work is allowed.

intentional_conflicts.this_value: the lead carries the pager one week in five
intentional_conflicts.other_value: hiring manager is leaning towards taking the lead off the pager rota (not approved)

must_not_infer: The job description gives no number of direct reports.
Nothing here mentions visa sponsorship, relocation assistance or a sign-on bonus.
Naming Duluth as the location does not by itself say whether remote work is possible; that is left to the location policy.
The range is a posted range, not a promise of where an offer will land.

files.title: Resume of Ottoline Vaskirk (candidate)

facts.statement: Ottoline Vaskirk lives in Madison, Wisconsin.
She has been Engineering Team Lead, Telemetry Pipeline at Halcyard Freight Cloud from March 2023 to the present; this is her only role with line management.
She leads and line-manages a team of 5 engineers at Halcyard.
Her team ingests sensor data from 22,000 trucks and trailers.
The resume says she contributed to the RabbitMQ-to-Kafka migration, a 9-engineer program led by the platform architect; it does not say she led it.
Within that migration she owned the consumer-side cutover for 14 services with no customer-facing downtime.
She reduced p99 ingestion latency from 4.2 s to 900 ms by redesigning partition keys and introducing micro-batching in the Go consumers.
She cut pipeline infrastructure spend by 23% ($410K annualized) through tiered retention and right-sizing brokers.
She was incident commander for 6 Sev-1 incidents across 2024 and 2025 and introduced blameless post-incident reviews.
She hired 3 engineers and supported one promotion to senior engineer.
Her pipeline's peak throughput is 38,000 messages per second.
She was Senior Software Engineer at Halcyard Freight Cloud from June 2020 to February 2023.

As Senior Software Engineer she built the change data capture pipeline from PostgreSQL into Kafka using Debezium, feeding Snowflake, with 140 tables replicated; this is the earliest Kafka work on the resume.
She wrote the Go client library that 11 internal services use to publish telemetry events.
As Senior Software Engineer she mentored 2 junior engineers with no line responsibility.
At Halcyard she took part in the on-call rotation one week in four.
She was Software Engineer at Pindrop & Wren Analytics in Milwaukee from August 2016 to May 2020, her first job on the resume.
At Pindrop & Wren she developed Java services and nightly Spark batch jobs for retail sales analytics; no streaming platform is listed for that job.
At Pindrop & Wren she cut the nightly batch runtime from 7 hours to 3.5 hours.
She holds a B.S. in Computer Science from the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire, 2016.
Her listed skills are Go, Java, Python, SQL; Kafka, RabbitMQ, Debezium, Spark, PostgreSQL, Snowflake; Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS.
doc_needles: Kafka, RabbitMQ, Debezium, Spark, PostgreSQL, Snowflake

facts.statement: She holds the AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate certification, 2021.
She gave the talk 'Cutting over 14 consumers without a maintenance window' at the Midwest Data Infrastructure Meetup in 2024.
Her summary says ten years in backend and data infrastructure, the last six in freight telemetry.
Outside work she mentors with Code Lantern and organises a streaming-systems reading group of about 30 people.

The resume does not say she used Kafka before June 2020; that is silence, not proof she did not.

files.title: Interview scorecard: Engineering Lead, Ingestion Platform

facts.statement: The scorecard for requisition ENG-2026-0417 is version 2, dated 4 September 2026, owned by hiring manager Idris Halvorsen-Peake and reviewed by Leopoldine Achterberg, Head of Talent.
Every interviewer rates all four dimensions and writes 'no evidence' rather than guessing.
Interviewers should use past-tense behavioral prompts rather than hypotheticals and record what the candidate did, not what the team did.
The rating scale runs from 1 (Does not meet) through 2 (Partially meets) and 3 (Meets) to 4 (Exceeds).
Technical depth in streaming systems carries 35% of the weighted score.
People leadership carries 30% of the weighted score.
Ownership and operational judgment carries 20% of the weighted score.
Communication carries 15% of the weighted score.
A candidate advances to the next stage when the weighted score is 3.0 or higher and no dimension is rated 1.
Must-have: streaming platform operations - has run a log-based streaming platform in production and can describe a failure they diagnosed themselves.
Must-have: direct people management - at least 2 years with line responsibility, including hiring, and has handled at least one underperformance case.
Must-have: incident command - has led the response to a customer-facing incident and the review afterwards.
Must-have: explaining trade-offs - can explain a design trade-off to a non-specialist in under two minutes.

Nice-to-have competencies are telematics or IoT device data, change data capture pipelines, cloud cost management for data infrastructure, and multi-region active-active deployments; they are never a reason to reject.
doc_needles: Cloud cost management for data infrastructure

facts.statement: A candidate who shows three or more of the nice-to-have competencies may be marked 'strong profile'.
doc_needles: three or more of the nice-to-have

facts.statement: A claim counts as verified when the candidate can state their own role, the size of the effort, one decision they personally made, and a measurable result.
When an answer stays at 'we', the interviewer asks for the candidate's own part.
doc_needles: ask for the candidate's own part

facts.statement: If something said in the interview differs from the resume, the interviewer notes both versions, asks the candidate to reconcile them, and does not assume which is right.
doc_needles: note both versions on the scorecard

facts.statement: Disqualifier: fewer than 2 years of direct people management; mentoring and tech-lead work without line responsibility do not count.
Disqualifier: cannot describe their own individual contribution to a project they claim, after two follow-up prompts.
Disqualifier: unwilling to take part in the on-call rotation.
Any disqualifier ends the process regardless of score; the interviewer records it and tells the hiring manager the same day.
Red flag (does not end the process; recorded and raised in the debrief): speaking dismissively about former colleagues or managers.
Red flag: sharing a former employer's confidential customer data.
Red flag: taking sole credit for a team outcome and not correcting it when asked who else was involved.
Per the scorecard, the panel recommendation is 'hire' when at least 3 of the 4 panel interviewers score the candidate 3.0 or above.

intentional_conflicts.this_value: hire when at least 3 of the 4 panel interviewers score 3.0 or above
intentional_conflicts.other_value: moves on only when all four panel interviewers recommend hire

must_not_infer: Red flags are not disqualifiers.
Nice-to-have competencies are never a reason to reject.
The scorecard does not say which of the two panel rules prevails.

files.title: Ingestion Platform: team brief for candidates

facts.statement: The team brief was last updated on 1 September 2026, prepared by Idris Halvorsen-Peake and cleared by People Operations for sharing with candidates.
Kestrelwick was founded in 2014 in Duluth, Minnesota and has about 310 employees.
Kestrelwick's product is Coldline, a routing and temperature-compliance platform for refrigerated freight.
Kestrelwick has 140 refrigerated carriers as customers in the United States and Canada, and roughly 61,000 trailers report into the platform.
Kestrelwick closed a Series D round of $85 million in May 2025, led by Tamarack Ridge Partners.
Kestrelwick's headquarters are in Duluth and it has an engineering hub in Chattanooga, Tennessee.
The Query Platform team is led by Tobiah Raskovic and has 6 engineers.
The Device Gateway team is led by Maribel Oyelaran-Fitch and has 5 engineers.
The Engineering Lead, Ingestion Platform has 4 direct reports: two senior engineers, one mid-level engineer and one associate engineer.
The Ingestion Platform team is based in Duluth.
doc_needles: The team is based in Duluth

facts.statement: One further senior engineer opening on the team is approved for the first quarter of 2027.
The lead reports to Idris Halvorsen-Peake, Director of Data Platform.
doc_needles: The lead reports to Idris Halvorsen-Peake

facts.statement: Idris Halvorsen-Peake reports to Yevgenia Marlowe-Okafor, VP of Engineering.
The role is open because the previous lead, Maribel Oyelaran-Fitch, moved in July 2026 to start the Device Gateway team; she is still in the group and has offered to hand over in person.
The team's services are written in Go; Python is used for tooling and data-quality jobs.
The team runs Apache Kafka, self-managed on Kubernetes, in three clusters.
The team uses ClickHouse for time-series storage and PostgreSQL for metadata.
The platform runs on AWS with us-east-2 as the primary region, with Terraform and Grafana.
On a normal weekday the platform takes in about 1.9 billion messages.
The platform's peak is around 52,000 messages per second, during the afternoon dispatch window.
The median delay from a trailer sending a reading to it being queryable is 4 seconds.
2027 priority: retire the legacy Sparrow batch importer by March 2027.
2027 priority: move Kafka to tiered storage, targeting 30% lower storage spend.
2027 priority: stand up a second ingestion region, us-west-2, by the third quarter of 2027.
The team runs two-week sprints, has standup at 9:30 Central and ships about 25 production deploys a week.
Engineers are levelled E1 to E7 and this role is an E6.
Recruiters may share everything in the brief but must not share revenue, runway, customer contract values or non-public customer names; those go to the hiring manager at the next stage.

must_not_infer: Nothing here gives revenue, runway, valuation or customer contract values.
The sizes of the Query Platform (6) and Device Gateway (5) teams are not the size of the Ingestion Platform team.
The brief says the team is based in Duluth; it does not state office days or remote eligibility.
The brief does not describe the on-call rotation.

files.title: Total Rewards Overview, version 4.1 (effective 1 March 2026)

facts.statement: The current Total Rewards overview is version 4.1, effective 1 March 2026, owned by People Operations (Marguerite Tso-Lindqvist).
Employees receive 24 days of PTO per year.
PTO accrues at 2 days per calendar month, starting with the month the employee joins, and can be used as it accrues.
Up to 5 unused PTO days carry into the next year.
Employees receive 10 sick days per year, separate from PTO.
Kestrelwick observes 11 company holidays.
The company closes from December 24 through January 1 and closure days are not deducted from PTO.
Every new parent receives 18 weeks of fully paid parental leave, whether through birth, adoption or foster placement.
Parental leave makes no distinction between primary and secondary caregivers.
doc_needles: no distinction between primary and secondary

facts.statement: Employees are eligible for parental leave after 90 days of employment and may take it in one or two blocks within the first year after the child arrives.
Kestrelwick is hybrid: employees whose home office is Duluth or Chattanooga are in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday; Monday and Friday are flexible.
Fully remote arrangements are limited to roles marked remote-eligible on the requisition, and people-manager roles are not remote-eligible.
New hires receive a one-time home-office setup allowance of $600; Duluth office parking is paid by the company.
Base pay is reviewed every April.
For lead and staff levels the annual bonus target is 12% of base salary.
For directors and above the annual bonus target is 18% of base salary.
Bonuses are paid in March for the previous calendar year and are prorated for a partial first year.

facts.statement: New hires receive a stock option grant that vests over four years: 25% after the first year, then monthly.
The size of the option grant is set at offer and depends on level; the overview gives no number.
Kestrelwick offers three medical plans and pays 90% of the employee premium and 70% of dependent premiums.
Dental and vision are fully paid for employees and coverage starts on the first day.

facts.statement: Employees on the high-deductible plan receive $1,000 a year into a health savings account.
Kestrelwick matches 401(k) contributions dollar for dollar up to 5% of salary and the match vests immediately.
The learning stipend is $2,000 per year.
The wellness allowance is $50 per month.

files.title: Engineering Recruiting Process Guide, version 2.3

facts.statement: The Engineering Recruiting Process Guide is version 2.3, effective 15 June 2026, owned by Leopoldine Achterberg, Head of Talent.
Every engineering hire goes through four stages: recruiter screen, hiring manager interview, panel loop, executive conversation.
The recruiter screen is 30 minutes by video.
The hiring manager interview is 60 minutes by video.
The panel loop is four 45-minute sessions in one day.
The panel loop has a 15-minute break after the second session.
For lead roles the panel sessions are system design, people leadership, incident retrospective and cross-functional partner.
The panel loop is held at the Duluth office or by video, whichever the candidate prefers.
The executive conversation is 30 minutes with the VP of Engineering.
There is no take-home exercise at any stage; it was removed from the engineering process in 2026.
doc_needles: no take-home exercise at any stage

facts.statement: A typical process runs three to four weeks from the recruiter screen to a decision.
After the recruiter screen and after the hiring manager interview, the recruiter gives the candidate an outcome within 2 business days.
The panel debrief is held within 2 business days of the panel loop.
The candidate is told the outcome of the panel within 3 business days after the debrief.
A written offer follows a verbal offer within 1 business day, and offers stay open for 5 business days.
Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding company holidays.
doc_needles: Business days are Monday to Friday

facts.statement: Per the process guide, a candidate moves on to the executive conversation only when all four panel interviewers recommend hire.
doc_needles: all four panel interviewers recommend hire

facts.statement: The recruiter chairs the panel debrief and records the outcome.
Two professional references are checked after the executive conversation and before any offer.
Offers are approved by the hiring manager and the VP of Engineering.
An offer with base pay above the midpoint of the posted range also needs sign-off from Total Rewards.
Base pay outside the posted range needs the approval of the VP of Engineering and the Head of People Operations before it is mentioned to a candidate.
doc_needles: Base pay outside the posted range

facts.statement: New hires start on the first or third Monday of a month.
A background check runs after the offer is accepted and usually takes about a week.
Recruiters share the posted base salary range in the first conversation if the candidate asks.
doc_needles: Share the posted base salary range

facts.statement: Recruiters may share the Total Rewards overview and the team brief freely; both are cleared for candidates.
Recruiters do not ask about current or past pay; they ask what the candidate is expecting instead.
Recruiters do not promise an offer, a level, a start date, pay outside the posted range, or an exception to any policy; they say what the process is and who decides.
The recruiter sends the candidate a follow-up email the same day, summarising next steps.
The recruiter submits the scorecard within 24 hours of the conversation.
The recruiter keeps the candidate record in Greenhollow current and moves the stage within 1 business day of an outcome.
For a panel loop at the Duluth office, the recruiting coordinator books and pays for travel and one hotel night directly.
Meals on the panel day are reimbursed up to $75 per day against receipts.
Candidates who are not selected are told by phone or video and may re-apply after 6 months.
Feedback is offered to anyone who reached the panel loop.
Scheduling and travel are handled by Bartholomew Nkemelu, Recruiting Coordinator.

files.title: Hiring manager's informal notes to the recruiter, 28 September 2026

facts.statement: These are informal notes from Idris Halvorsen-Peake to the recruiter, written on Monday 28 September 2026.
Idris wants the recruiter to probe the Kafka migration: the resume says 'contributed' while her meetup talk bio suggests she ran it; ask what she personally decided.
Idris wants one real case of her managing someone out or coaching an underperformer.
Idris wants to know whether she is still writing Go or has only been in meetings since becoming lead.
Idris does not know why she is leaving Halcyard and asks the recruiter to find out.
Idris is leaning towards taking the lead off the pager rota once the new senior hire lands, but has not cleared it with Yevgenia, the JD is unchanged, and it must not be floated to candidates.
Idris would argue for the upper half of the range if she is as good as her resume, but Yevgenia signs.
Idris hopes to have someone signed by mid-November; he says it is a hope, not a promise.
For the panel Idris has asked Tobiah to take system design and Maribel the incident retro; the cross-functional interviewer, probably from Customer Operations, is not yet set.
Idris notes she is in Madison, does not know whether she would move, and treats where people work from as a People Ops matter.
Maribel has said she will give the new lead two weeks of overlap.
Idris says the team brief is up to date and should be used for roadmap topics.
